passage: Four teams were building science models for the fair, and each leader steered differently. Nilesh's team wrote down research, materials, building and presentation, gave each member the job that suited their strengths, and set a date for every stage. Jaya, another leader, saw that painting could not begin until the frame dried and that testing needed a circuit that already worked. So she started those linked jobs first and let the separate ones run beside them. Deepak trusted nobody with the work. He did most of it at night and grew exhausted, the team felt pushed aside, the quality fell, and the others learned nothing from the project. After the model failed at the fair, Meena asked each member to name one worry. She then scored the ideas for money, hours and whether they could be done, so the next decision rested on evidence rather than on who sounded most sure.

qa.q: What did Nilesh's team set for every stage?
qa.a: They set a date for every stage.

qa.q: How does Deepak's way of leading differ from Nilesh's, and what happened to the teams?
qa.a: Deepak did most of the work himself, so he was exhausted, quality fell and the team learned nothing. Nilesh gave each member a task that matched their strengths and set dates, so everyone took part.

qa.q: What might the members of Deepak's team be feeling?
qa.a: They probably feel sidelined and unimportant, because Deepak did the work himself and did not trust them.

qa.q: What could Deepak try to work better with his team?
qa.a: He could give each member a clear job, check in on progress, and listen to their concerns, as Meena did. Sharing the work would also stop him being exhausted. 🙂

grounding: Team leaders manage a group project by assigning tasks, ordering dependent work, doing everything alone, and inviting concerns to decide by criteria.
